mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In a robustness check, the interaction term (PAYEMS * -UNRATE) shows a p-value > 0.10 for 20-day returns after controlling for macroeconomic factors.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures ( proxy via GDPC1 ) exceeding 2% for two consecutive months predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates continued consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by > 2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 growth is below 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month is interpreted as a supply shock that raises uncertainty, lowering S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5% in a single month
failure_condition: During supply disruptions, the 20-day forward return is not significantly different from the pre-shock average (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.5% in a month, it indicates inflationary pressure that the Fed may combat with rate hikes, which tends to depress equity valuations and produce negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.5% in a single month
failure_condition: In periods of actual Fed rate hikes following such CPI moves, the 60-day forward return is not statistically different from the prior 60-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for three consecutive months, without a corresponding rise in jobless claims (PAYEMS), suggests a tight labor market that supports economic expansion and positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% for three consecutive months and PAYEMS does not increase sharply
failure_condition: The interaction between UNRATE and PAYEMS shows a non-significant positive effect on 20-day returns (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in retail sales volume proxies (not directly available, so this sketch is invalid per instructions) — instead, use HOUST as a proxy for business activity. A monthly decline in HOUST by 4% signals weakening demand, leading to negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by > 4% in a month
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when HOUST declines by < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a post-pandemic recovery phase (regime_hint: 'post-pandemic recovery') is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return, regardless of the direction of FEDFUNDS or UNRATE, due to reduced policy uncertainty and improved growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: regime: 'post-pandemic recovery' detected (e.g., UNRATE < 4% for 6 months with upward trend)
failure_condition: In the identified regime, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during the pre-recovery baseline (p > 0.05).
